Chelpis showcases post-quantum security solutions at Semicon Taiwan
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-02
09:20:12 UTC
18:20:12 KST

TAIPEI (Taiwan News) — Taiwan cybersecurity company Chelpis is showcasing post-quantum cryptography technologies spanning semiconductor chips, firmware, communications, and autonomous systems at Semicon Taiwan.
The global technology industry is preparing for the transition to security standards designed to withstand attacks from quantum computers. To assist with this transition, the company is presenting an array of technologies aimed at semiconductor and financial systems, AI data centers, drones, and autonomous robots, per a press release.
Chelpis is exhibiting on the fourth floor in Hall 1 at the Taipei Nangang Exhibition Center until Friday. The company said the semiconductor industry's long product lifecycles make it increasingly important to incorporate quantum-resistant security at the chip-design stage rather than treating it as a software upgrade later.
Chelpis Founder and CEO Chih Ming-yang (池明洋) said the shift toward post-quantum security represents both a new technical requirement and a business opportunity for the semiconductor supply chain.
“Quantum-safe security is no longer just a future consideration,” the company said, describing its technology as designed to protect systems against both current and future cryptographic threats.
Security closer to the chip
One of Chelpis' main exhibits is its Quantum-Safe Root of Trust (QoT) technology, which incorporates a hardware-based PQC Secure Enclave into chip and system-on-chip architectures. The company said the technology combines protected PQC cryptographic processing cores with dedicated memory, allowing manufacturers to incorporate quantum-safe security into products from the earliest stages of chip design.
Chelpis said the approach is particularly relevant to products with long operating lifecycles, including automotive electronics, industrial control systems, defense technology, edge AI devices, and other smart devices.
The company also promotes the technology as a defense against so-called “harvest now, decrypt later” attacks, in which encrypted data is collected today with the expectation that future advances in quantum computing could eventually make it possible to decrypt the information.
The US National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) finalized its first three PQC standards in 2024 — FIPS 203, FIPS 204 and FIPS 205. The standards cover key establishment and digital signatures designed to resist attacks by quantum computers.
NIST has continued expanding its PQC work. In March 2025, it selected the HQC algorithm as a backup encryption algorithm to ML-KEM, while advising organizations to continue migrating to the standards finalized in 2024.
PQC for drones and robots
Chelpis is also demonstrating applications for autonomous unmanned systems, including drones, quadruped robots and other autonomous machines. The company said the security challenge for such systems extends beyond protecting stored data. Command authority, device identity, control instructions, and real-time video transmissions also need protection against interception or manipulation.
Its PQ-SDN, PQConnect, and PQTunnel technologies are designed to establish post-quantum-secure communications across multiple network protocols, including distributed and mesh-network environments. Chelpis said its PQC technology has already been deployed in the nation’s drone industry to encrypt communications between flight controllers and ground control stations, protecting flight-control commands and video data.
Chelpis will present “Quantum-Safe in Autonomous Robots" at Semicon Taiwan's TechXPOT stage at 2:40 p.m. Friday in Area L on the fourth floor of TaiNEX 1. The presentation will examine how PQC can be incorporated into autonomous robots' devices, communications, and control architectures, as well as how semiconductor suppliers can prepare for the global transition to quantum-safe security, per the press release.
The company said it is also working on PQC migration services covering cryptographic asset inventories, risk assessments, migration planning, and deployment. Chelpis describes its product portfolio as covering three areas: PQ-IC for quantum-safe chip technologies, PQ-UxV for unmanned vehicles, and PQ-AI data center technologies for AI infrastructure.
Chelpis said it was the first company in Taiwan to receive certification under NIST's Cryptographic Algorithm Validation Program and that it has integrated NIST-standardized PQC algorithms into chip intellectual property and firmware-protection solutions.

The tour will also include information on local folklore and historical disaster-prevention practices, and will run from 10:30 a.m. to 12 noon. Register here.
Another activity is an exhibit on the history of Hamasen, a former urban hub for trade, transportation, and daily life. This exhibit portrays Hamasen as a “living system,” which is a continuously operating urban space that remains in use today, the bureau said. Visitors can rediscover its cultural heritage and see familiar streets from a new perspective.
National Heritage Day limited-edition stamps will be available at the exhibit, which will be held at Kaohsiung’s Former Patriotic Women’s Association Hall.
Finally, the public can interact with live actors at the old British Consulate at Takow in an immersive mystery game centering on the historical context of the Shaochuantou waterfront. Reserve a time here.

TAIPEI (Taiwan News) — Taoyuan International Airport Corporation confirmed on Wednesday that the Terminal 3 project will be completed by the end of 2027.
Corporation President Fan Hsiao-lun (范孝倫) said the project is a major national infrastructure undertaking, complex in scope. However, once finished, it will enhance the airport’s overall operational capacity, according to a company press release.
Fan said the company has continued to hire prosecutors, anti-corruption officials, investigators, and occupational safety units to strengthen external oversight and project transparency. Inviting outside groups to inspect the construction site allows the public to understand how transparency and efficiency are balanced while completing major projects, he said.
Fan added that cross-agency collaboration ensures construction efficiency and clean governance.
The terminal will be able to handle 45 million passengers a year. The airport said self-check-in counters will account for nearly half of check-in services at the new terminal. Staffed check-in counters will also be 60% to 70% longer than those at terminals 1 and 2, allowing passengers to check in baggage earlier and more smoothly.
The terminal will have 18 large elevators to help passengers move through the building. It will also include five gates for smaller aircraft.
Transportation Minister Chen Shih-kai (陳世凱) urged construction crews to speed up work after visiting the terminal in June. He also requested Taoyuan International Airport Corporation to implement measures to boost efficiency.
The north boarding concourse of Terminal 3, designed by British-Italian architect Richard Rogers, opened for trial operations in December.

Meta settlement could clear the way for new AI product launches, Morgan Stanley says
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-02
09:19:25 UTC
18:19:25 KST

Meta's $18 billion social media settlement lifts a legal overhang that some analysts say could clear the way for a wave of new AI product launches.
The tech giant went to trial in August after a lawsuit filed by 29 U.S. state attorneys general alleged that its platforms, Instagram and Facebook, had design features that posed harms to younger users.
In week two of the trial, Meta and the states agreed to a settlement in which Meta said it would make core changes to its platforms for users under 18. These range from a two-hour daily usage limit to disabling extreme makeup and cosmetic surgery filters and introducing tighter age verification measures.
The outcome raised investor concerns about reduced advertising revenue, and analysts at Morgan Stanley said that substantial lawsuits often drive tech giants to release innovative new products and offerings.
"We see multiple new products in the pipeline from Meta (MetaClaw/a better MetaAI, a full suite of agentic ad tooling for small to medium-sized businesses, upcoming rollout of new subscription offerings, a robust API offering, neocloud optionality and more)," they said in a Saturday note. They added that they're not claiming Meta's products are ready for launch.
Meta is reportedly set to release its consumer AI agent Hatch in early September, which will run inside its platforms WhatsApp and Instagram, and can perform autonomous tasks including online purchases and restaurant bookings, according to an internal memo seen by Business Insider.
A "slew of successful new product and model launches" followed the Department of Justice's decision to rule against a forced sale of Google's key assets last year, the Morgan Stanley analysts said. Those product launches included "Gemini 3 and broader rollout of search tools including AI Mode/AI Overviews," which also lifted its valuation.
"There are certainly signals, in our view, that Meta's product pipeline could start flowing following this legal clearing event… just like Google's last year," they added.
Investment bank Needham maintained its "hold" rating on Meta stock after the settlement.
It noted Meta's costly "strategy diffusion," which includes expanding simultaneously into custom chips, data center infrastructure, enterprise AI software, business agents, model APIs, compute sales, advertising tools, consumer assistants, smart glasses and other hardware.
"By not concentrating its capital and free cash flow on the highest-return products and services, it raises the risk that management attention, engineering talent and shareholder capital are spread across too many things, and lowers the likelihood that Meta succeeds at any of them, we believe," the Needham analysts added in Aug. 27 note.
Morgan Stanley: Teens make up only 1% of Meta's revenue
Meta will pay out the billion-dollar settlement in the social media case over ten years, and said it's booking a $10 billion legal charge in its third quarter this year following the outcome of the trial.
The guidance the company provided in July otherwise remains unchanged, following the settlement.
One of the conditions of paying out the full settlement is that rivals YouTube and TikTok make similar changes to their apps for younger users.
Enforcing youth engagement ceilings may pose a "larger long-term headwind" for YouTube than for Meta, as youth adoption of YouTube is higher than for Facebook or Instagram, the Morgan Stanley analysts said.
"We also believe revenue from teens represents only ~1% of META revenue," they added.
However, the Needham analysts pointed out that "the timing of payments couldn't be worse," as Meta expects up to $145 billion of capital expenditure in 2026 as it races to come out on top in the AI buildout.
The settlement and compliance costs could add to the company's growing cost pressures.

The participation of these large defense contractors in SAHA Istanbul’s management and committees also enables closer integration with more than 1,300 small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) within the cluster.
The production capacity of these SMEs provides larger defense companies with more flexible supply chains, helps shorten delivery times and strengthens the global competitiveness of Türkiye’s defense industry.

Russian President Vladimir Putin said Moscow would “find a way to respond” if civilian “tragedies” followed President Volodymyr Zelenskyy’s warning that Ukrainian drone operations were making Russian skies unsafe. Zelenskyy told foreign airlines and insurers that the “safe moments” in Russian airspace were over.
Zelenskyy’s warning seeks to extend the cost of Russia’s war beyond damaged military and energy facilities to airlines, insurers, and travelers. It does not mean Russian airspace is legally or completely closed. However, carriers that continue flying over Russia face higher costs from repeated airport shutdowns during drone alerts, as well as the danger that military activity in Russian airspace could endanger civilian aircraft.
Putin spoke after a 1 September Shanghai Cooperation Organization summit in Bishkek, where Russia and China coordinate regional security. Zelenskyy’s warning amounted to “a bid for state terrorism” if he had made it publicly, the Russian president said, adding that Russia does not negotiate with “terrorists.” Putin also said Russian forces were preparing massive strikes on Ukraine’s energy infrastructure.
In his evening video address, Zelenskyy said Ukraine did not threaten civilian aircraft but would keep striking Russian military targets and parts of the economy supporting the war. Ukraine’s Presidential Office head Kyrylo Budanov backed the decision, saying long-range weapons would systematically strike military targets in Russia while the invasion continued.
“Russian airspace will effectively be closing”: Zelenskyy warns airlines Russian skies are no longer safe
Shares in Aeroflot, Russia’s national airline, fell to an intraday low of 30.36 rubles at about 20:40 Moscow time, down 5.11%, Meduza reported, citing Moscow Exchange data. The timing does not establish that Zelenskyy’s speech alone drove the decline.
Wall Street Journal correspondent Yaroslav Trofimov posted a chart of the decline on X, writing, “Aeroflot shares after Zelensky’s warning.”

Previous closures of Russian airspace due to Ukrainian attacks
Russian airports were repeatedly shut during Ukrainian drone alerts well before Zelenskyy’s warning. On 6 July 2025, Moscow airports canceled 171 flights while airports in five other cities suspended operations.
A 27 May attack closed airports serving Moscow and several other cities after Russia claimed it intercepted 99 drones. Another wave caused flight disruption and mobile internet outages around Moscow, while a 29 May alert again halted flights at Moscow airports.

Serco wins RAF Fylingdales radar support contract
United Kingdom
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-02
10:17:22 BST
18:17:22 KST

Serco has been awarded a five-year Ministry of Defence contract to continue operating, maintaining and sustaining the early warning radar at RAF Fylingdales in North Yorkshire, according to the company.
The contract, awarded by the National Armaments Director Group, covers the Solid State Phased Array Radar, or SSPAR, which forms part of the UK and US governments’ Upgraded Early Warning Radar network.
The new agreement will begin in April 2027 and includes an option for a further two-year extension.
RAF Fylingdales provides missile warning and space surveillance functions, with the radar designed to detect and track missiles as part of the US Missile Defence ground-based radar network. Serco provides continuous support at the site 24 hours a day, 365 days a year. Under the new contract it will remain responsible for radar hardware, systems operation and maintenance, alongside analytical and training activities.
The company said the Fylingdales team is also involved in tracking objects in Low Earth Orbit. During 2025, the SSPAR completed more than 5.9 million tracks of satellites in Low Earth Orbit, with Serco personnel providing real-time analysis of satellite break-ups, re-entries, new launches and manoeuvres.
Anthony Kirby, Serco Group Chief Executive, said: “We are immensely proud of our dedicated team at RAF Fylingdales who are entrusted to seamlessly deliver this continuous service, helping to defend the nation and protect our skies.”
He added: “We have a long history over sixty years supporting the UK Space Command, US Space Force and the Royal Air Force at RAF Fylingdales, with our people at the heart of this critical infrastructure asset.”
Kirby said: “Our success in securing this contract reflects the strength of our expertise and growing capabilities in defence and builds on our recent strong momentum.”
The contract will also introduce a new Serco-developed analytical system known as the Enhanced Spacetrack Processor, or ESP. The software will be used to analyse large volumes of tracking data to determine the position, orbit and size of objects in Low Earth Orbit. Serco developed ESP with the Royal Air Force and UK Space Command. It will replace the United Kingdom Spacetrack Processor, another Serco-developed system which has been used for more than three decades.
The company will also provide apprenticeships during the contract period. These will include Level 3 opportunities for school and college leavers and Level 5 and 6 apprenticeships for existing employees. Serco has partnered with Teesside University and Redcar & Cleveland College to develop an apprenticeship specifically for RAF Fylingdales, covering skills and qualifications relevant to work at the site.

====================================================================================================

This is what the post-Western world looks like
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-02
09:17:06 UTC
18:17:06 KST

This is what the post-Western world looks like
The Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) summit in Bishkek will be remembered less for its formal group photo than for the leaders in attendance – and the political significance of bringing them together. Seated around the same table were Russian President Vladimir Putin, Chinese President Xi Jinping, Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, and the leaders of Central Asian nations, Iran, Pakistan, and Belarus. They were joined for the expanded session by leaders of partner countries, including Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, as well as representatives of international organizations, among them UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres.
This was no longer simply a regional gathering focused on security in Central Asia. The SCO’s ten member states now cover roughly a quarter of the world’s landmass, account for more than 42% of its population, and generate over 23% of global GDP. In other words, nearly half of humanity was represented in Bishkek. The simultaneous presence of the leaders of Russia, China, and India was especially significant: They represent the world’s largest country by area, its second-largest economy, and its most populous nation. Together with the SCO’s other members, they form a demographic, resource, industrial, and political bloc without which any serious discussion of reshaping the international order is now impossible.
That is why the summit in Kyrgyzstan should be seen as more than another entry on the diplomatic calendar. It demonstrated that multipolarity is no longer an abstract formula but is beginning to acquire a clear institutional shape. The SCO is one of the platforms where a new balance of power is emerging not only in speeches and declarations, but in practice – through regular meetings between leaders, security coordination, settlements in national currencies, new transportation corridors, energy cooperation, and the gradual development of independent mechanisms for growth.
From the Shanghai Five to Greater Eurasia
Over the past quarter-century, the SCO has evolved from a confidence-building mechanism along the former Soviet-Chinese border into the largest association in Greater Eurasia. Its original agenda – combating terrorism, separatism, and extremism – remains in place, but it is no longer the organization’s sole focus. Trade, energy, transportation, digitalization, food security, humanitarian exchanges, and the reform of international institutions have all been added to the list.
The Bishkek summit cemented that evolution. The leaders adopted the Bishkek Declaration along with 27 other documents. The package included decisions on responding to emerging security challenges, combating drug trafficking, developing ports and logistics hubs, nuclear safety, energy, and emergency response. The SCO also introduced a single partner status, merging the previously separate categories of observer state and dialogue partner. On the surface, this may look like an administrative reform. Its political significance, however, is much broader: The organization is streamlining its external framework and preparing for more systematic engagement with countries that want to cooperate without immediately becoming full members.
The practical side of multipolarity is also visible in the economic sphere. Putin said national currencies now account for more than 98% of Russia’s settlements with other SCO countries. This does not yet amount to a common currency or a unified financial system, but it points to a sustained trend: The organization’s members are seeking to reduce their mutual trade’s dependence on external payment infrastructure. Discussions about an SCO Development Bank, new investment instruments, and the integration of Eurasian transportation routes are part of the same effort.
At the same time, the SCO’s emergence as a genuine center of global politics will depend on how quickly it can turn declarations into working projects. The organization already possesses immense collective potential, but there is always a gap between potential and real influence. Final communiqués alone will not close it. Banks, transportation routes, payment systems, security centers, and resilient trade networks will.
SCO Plus: Expanding without endlessly adding members
The defining political development of the Bishkek summit was the consolidation of the SCO Plus format. The first summit-level meeting under that name was held in Astana in 2024. In Bishkek, it moved beyond the experimental stage and became a distinct element of the summit itself. Representatives of 17 countries and six international organizations took part in the SCO and SCO Plus events. The expanded session focused on the role of the United Nations and the SCO countries’ contribution to building a fair multipolar world order.
The logic closely resembles that of BRICS Plus. In both cases, the goal is to build a broad circle of partners around a permanent core. This model allows the organization to expand its geographic reach without turning the admission of new members into an endless process or overburdening its decision-making machinery. Countries can participate in discussions of major issues, advance economic and political initiatives, and develop ties with members while retaining their freedom of maneuver.
There is, however, a difference between the two formats. BRICS Plus is primarily focused on the global economy, development, and reform of international financial governance. SCO Plus has emerged from a Eurasian agenda centered on security, transportation connectivity, and political dialogue. Over time, the two mechanisms could complement one another: BRICS can provide the broader global framework, while the SCO builds a dense network of cooperation across Greater Eurasia.
Türkiye’s participation in the meeting was particularly revealing. Ankara remains an SCO partner rather than a full member, while also belonging to NATO and pursuing an independent policy in Eurasia. Its presence demonstrates that the SCO does not force its partners to make a rigid geopolitical choice. Instead, it offers a platform to countries that do not want to confine themselves to a single bloc and are seeking to diversify their foreign relationships.
This is one of the defining features of the emerging multipolar system. It does not necessarily mean replacing the old closed camp with a new one. Rather, it is a system of overlapping formats in which countries can cooperate on some issues while disagreeing on others. SCO Plus is becoming the institutional expression of precisely that model.
Iran, Pakistan, and Türkiye: The SCO’s new geography
The presence of Iran, Pakistan, and Türkiye gives the SCO a significance that extends far beyond Central Asia. Their respective statuses, however, differ – and that distinction matters. Iran and Pakistan are full members: Islamabad joined alongside India in 2017, while Tehran completed the accession process in 2023. Türkiye participates in the SCO’s broader orbit as a partner.
The admission of Iran and Pakistan redrew the organization’s political map. It brought South Asia, Afghanistan, the Persian Gulf, and the Middle East directly into the SCO’s purview. At the same time, it brought together countries with serious disagreements of their own. That complicates efforts to forge a common position, but it also makes the organization more valuable. Dialogue is needed most not by those who already agree, but by those whose interests regularly collide.
In the Bishkek Declaration, the participants reaffirmed their support for Iran’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, condemned the military strikes on Iranian territory, and called for a political and diplomatic settlement of the conflict. This was an important outcome for Tehran. Iran’s SCO membership has acquired practical value by allowing the country to place its own security on the collective political agenda of a major Eurasian organization.
Pakistan’s role is equally significant. Islamabad is not an invited participant but a full member – and Pakistan will assume the SCO chairmanship after Kyrgyzstan. This underscores the organization’s shift from its original Central Asian core toward a broader Eurasian configuration. The simultaneous membership of India and Pakistan does not eliminate their disputes, but it preserves a common channel of communication even during periods of severe tension.
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian’s remarks at the SCO Plus session captured the central meaning of the gathering. The emerging order, he argued, must not amount to replacing one center of hegemony with another. Multipolarity can be fair only if it rests on sovereign equality, multilateralism, and international law. This is an important caveat: Simply increasing the number of power centers does not automatically make the international system more stable. It also requires rules, representative institutions, and mechanisms for reconciling competing interests. Pezeshkian separately emphasized the potential of SCO Plus as a platform for shaping the future international order.
This also explains the criticism of the effectiveness of the UN and its Security Council voiced in Bishkek. SCO countries are not proposing that the United Nations be abandoned. On the contrary, they insist that it must retain its central role. But that role should be supported by updated representation that reflects the actual distribution of political, economic, and demographic weight in the world. Otherwise, the gap between the formal architecture of the mid-20th century and the realities of the 21st will only continue to widen.
Russia’s opportunity: A bridge, not an arbiter
For Russia, the Bishkek summit mattered not only because it reaffirmed the country’s place among Eurasia’s leading power centers. Moscow possesses a rare network of relationships that allows it to serve as a bridge between different groups within the SCO. Russia has a strategic partnership with China, a special and privileged partnership with India, stable ties with Pakistan, allied relations with the countries of Central Asia, a comprehensive strategic partnership with Iran, and an ongoing political dialogue with Türkiye.
This network gives Moscow an opportunity to help resolve conflicts and reduce tensions. That does not mean turning the SCO into a supranational court or imposing ready-made solutions on its members. The organization operates by consensus, and bilateral disputes have traditionally been kept out of the center of its formal agenda. Russia’s most realistic role is therefore to offer its good offices, keep channels of communication open, facilitate informal consultations, encourage confidence-building measures, and create conditions in which direct dialogue becomes possible.
The historical parallel is obvious. In 1966, Soviet mediation led to the signing of the Tashkent Declaration, which brought an end to the 1965 war between India and Pakistan. That experience cannot simply be transplanted into the present day, but it serves as a reminder that Moscow can be useful to both sides precisely because it maintains working relations with both New Delhi and Islamabad.
A similar approach could be applied to other flashpoints, from tensions surrounding Iran and security in the Persian Gulf to Afghanistan and border disputes in Asia. Russia’s contribution could be to translate the SCO’s general commitment to political and diplomatic conflict resolution into specific mechanisms: contact groups, expert consultations, communication channels between military officials and diplomats, joint threat assessments, and agreements to protect transportation and energy infrastructure.
The organization’s capabilities should not be overstated, however. The SCO is not a military-political bloc, does not impose alliance discipline, and brings together countries with very different concepts of security. The Kashmir conflict between India and Pakistan remains unresolved, India and China continue to have border disputes, and the members’ positions on many international crises do not always align. Yet the SCO’s ability to keep these countries within a common negotiating framework is itself one of its most important assets.
A multipolar world is not a world of universal agreement. It is an order in which no single power center can dictate the rules on its own, forcing states to construct a complex system of compromises. The SCO fits this logic better than many traditional alliances: It does not demand ideological conformity, impose a single model of development, or require its members to rally against a common enemy.
The bottom line from Bishkek
The summit’s most important outcome was that the SCO has definitively moved beyond seeing itself solely as a regional security organization. The Bishkek Declaration, deeper financial and transportation cooperation, the new unified partner status, and the consolidation of the SCO Plus format are creating a broader framework – political, economic, and, most importantly, institutional.
An impressive geographic reach alone does not guarantee effectiveness. The SCO still needs to accelerate the development of project-financing mechanisms, give its new security centers substantive responsibilities, improve transportation links, and learn to play a more active role in de-escalating tensions among its own members. But the direction of travel is already clear.
Bishkek presented multipolarity not as a slogan but as a political reality. Russia, China, and India were in the same room; Iran and Pakistan participated as full members; Türkiye attended as a key partner in the expanded format. These countries do not constitute a unified bloc, nor do they seek to subsume their individual interests into a common line. But they are creating a space in which security, development, and global governance can be discussed without outside supervision or compulsory submission to a single center of power.
In this sense, SCO Plus is more than a successful adaptation of the BRICS model. It is a bid to build an open political framework around Greater Eurasia. If the organization can translate its demographic and economic scale into functioning institutions, platforms like this will shape not only the debate about a multipolar world, but also the way that world operates in practice.

Ukrainians injured in explosion at German railway station
A local media outlet has reported that two Ukrainians were injured in an explosion at Augsburg Central Station in Bavaria on the morning of 2 September.
Source: European Pravda, citing North Swabia police on X (Twitter)
Details: The explosion occurred in a passageway inside the station building near a bank. Two people sustained minor injuries. Windows were also damaged.
Local newspaper Presse Augsburg reported that a 17-year-old girl and an 18-year-old man who were injured in the attack are Ukrainian citizens.
Law enforcement officers cordoned off the station building and platform one. All the other platforms remained in operation for some time, while passengers were advised to use the station's southern and northern entrances.
Police later announced that the entire station building had been closed after a suspicious object was discovered. Train services were suspended.
Officers from the Bavarian State Criminal Police Office were called to the scene to investigate. Police said it is not yet clear what the object was and exactly how the explosion occurred.
Background:
- A suspicious incident occurred on the night of 1-2 September at an electrical substation near Cologne. Police suspect foul play and are looking into a possible connection to a recent act of sabotage in Brandenburg, where an attempt was made to damage the state's largest power plant.
- Oleksii Makeiev, Ukraine's Ambassador to Germany, said Kyiv works closely with Berlin to help Germany counter Russian sabotage.

China cracks down on AI ‘slop’, clearing out clutter from WeChat, RedNote, Douyin
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-02

18:15:21 KST

Advertisement
China cracks down on AI ‘slop’, clearing out clutter from WeChat, RedNote, Douyin
Clampdown sweeps across 2,400 websites and apps as cyberspace watchdog escalates fight against generative tech abuse
1-MIN READ1-MIN
 Listen
Ben Jiangin Beijing
China is cracking down on artificial intelligence-generated “slop” – low-grade, mass-produced synthetic content cluttering social media and news feeds – as part of a sweeping campaign against the abuse of the generative technology, the country’s top internet watchdog said on Wednesday.
In a statement posted to its website, the Cyberspace Administration of China (CAC) said it had scrubbed more than 5.61 million pieces of harmful or illegal content and removed some 49,000 accounts during its latest enforcement drive.
The clampdown swept up 2,400 websites and apps, targeting some of China’s biggest digital spaces, including TikTok’s sister app Douyin and rival Kuaishou, as well as RedNote and Tencent Holdings’ WeChat.
Authorities focused on reining in AI-driven fake news, explicit and violent material, impersonation and safety violations involving minors.
The response underscores Beijing’s growing concerns over the accessibility of generative AI. As tools become cheaper and more sophisticated, creators can produce convincing deepfakes and clickbait in seconds, challenging existing moderation systems.
The CAC said creators on Douyin, Kuaishou and WeChat used AI to turn literary classics such as Romance of the Three Kingdoms and Journey to the West into sensationalised, low-grade “digital swill” to attract traffic.

Daily Update: Russia Loses 1,390 Troops and 62 Artillery Systems in One Day

According to the latest Ukrainian military figures, Russia’s total personnel losses since the start of its full-scale invasion on February 24, 2022, have reached approximately 1,491,030.
We bring you stories from the ground. Your support keeps our team in the field.
Russian forces also lost six armored combat vehicles over the latest reporting period, bringing their estimated cumulative losses to 12,324 tanks and 25,263 armored combat vehicles.
Russia’s total artillery losses have risen to 49,016 systems after another 62 were recorded over the past day. Ukraine also reported the loss of two Russian multiple-launch rocket systems and one air defense system, bringing those totals to 2,081 and 1,598, respectively.
Estimated Russian aviation losses remain unchanged at 440 aircraft and 354 helicopters.
The General Staff also reported that Russia lost 12 unmanned ground systems over the past day, raising cumulative losses in that category to 2,464.
Another 1,969 operational-tactical UAVs were recorded as lost during the latest 24-hour period, bringing the overall figure to 494,146.
Ukraine also reported 10 Russian cruise missiles lost over the past day, raising Russia’s estimated cumulative losses in that category to 5,070.
Russia’s other estimated losses stand at 35 ships and boats, two submarines, 142,715 vehicles and fuel tankers, and 4,625 pieces of special equipment. Over the latest reporting period, Russian forces lost another 383 vehicles and fuel tankers and two pieces of special equipment.
Meanwhile, Ukrainian and Russian forces clashed 213 times across the front over the previous day.
Russia carried out one missile strike and 93 airstrikes, dropping 313 guided aerial bombs, according to the General Staff. Russian forces also deployed 11,511 strike drones and conducted 2,969 strikes against Ukrainian positions and populated areas, including 57 involving multiple-launch rocket systems.
Earlier, reports emerged that Russian forces lost 124,170 personnel on the battlefield during the three summer months of 2026, including more than 42,000 in August.
According to the General Staff, Russian personnel losses amounted to 39,290 in June, increased to 42,860 in July, and reached 42,020 in August.

Russia Honors Soldier Listed on Pedophilia Watchlist as New School Year “Hero”
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-02
09:15:05 UTC
18:15:05 KST

- Category
- World
Russia Honors Soldier Listed on Pedophilia Watchlist as New School Year “Hero”
On September 2, schools across the Komi Republic will hold lesson events dedicated to Corporal Alexander Vlasenkov, who died in Ukraine and was posthumously awarded the Hero of Russia title by Vladimir Putin, according to The Insider.
Vlasenkov, who was heavily promoted by former Putin bodyguard Alexander Matovnikov, was honored with monuments, plaques, and a school museum. However, investigation details reveal that Vlasenkov was registered on a special police watch list for pedophilia and fled to the front lines to escape law enforcement supervision and debts totaling 900,000 rubles ($12,200).
We bring you stories from the ground. Your support keeps our team in the field.
Former junior hand-to-hand combat champion Alexander Vlasenkov accumulated significant debts in 2019–2021, including 500,000 rubles ($6,800) in personal loans and nearly 400,000 rubles ($5,400) borrowed using his grandmother’s passport.
He avoided traveling for sports demonstrations due to fears of being detained at airport security checkpoints. Concurrently, police regularly conducted checks on him because he was registered on a special police watch list as a pedophile following an incident during his second year at the St. Petersburg University of the Ministry of Internal Affairs, where he attempted to assault a 13-year-old teenager before being interrupted by passersby.
To avoid a public scandal, the university administration expelled Vlasenkov, and he avoided imprisonment by completing mandatory military service in the Air Defense Forces.
According to The Insider, After completing his service in 2019, he worked briefly as a youth coach in Irkutsk until local police notified the school administration of his record, forcing him to return to his hometown of Chim. There, he worked as an electrician while occasionally assisting with sports training under the supervision of a local officer.
In early 2022, facing financial hardship, Vlasenkov sought loans from family and his former coach before traveling to Moscow to seek assistance from the International Hand-to-Hand Combat Federation. He met with General Alexander Matovnikov, deputy commander-in-chief of the Russian Ground Forces, who advised him to join the military as a volunteer.
Russian legislation prohibiting individuals suspected of sex crimes involving minors from signing military contracts was not enacted until 2024. Vlasenkov subsequently served as a scout-sniper in the 200th Separate Motor Rifle Brigade of the Northern Fleet and was killed on September 2, 2022, near the village of Udy in the Kharkiv region.
Following his death, Matovnikov promoted Vlasenkov’s story through state media and official channels to establish a patriotic narrative. On October 22, 2022, a presidential decree awarded Vlasenkov the Hero of Russia title posthumously, with the award presented to his family by regional officials.
Sources within the presidential administration noted that high-volume award submissions from the Ministry of Defense undergo reduced background checks during active operations, allowing individuals with criminal records or active police files to receive top national honors.
Local authorities subsequently named streets and opened museum displays in Vlasenkov's memory, while state media produced a televised documentary portraying his final actions in combat. The documentary omitted his police record and financial debts, focusing instead on his athletic background and military service, as reported by The Insider.
A similar case involved Andrey Kiyko, a convicted serial killer known as the “Sosnovka Maniac,” signed a military service contract with Russia’s Ministry of Defense despite official claims that prisoners convicted of sexual violence would not be recruited.
Kiyko had been convicted of two murders, multiple sexual assaults, and 11 robberies committed in St. Petersburg between 2004 and 2007, with an additional murder conviction in 2023 extending his sentence to 25 years.
After being wounded in January 2025, he was transferred to a Kronstadt rehabilitation facility, from which he escaped later that year. The Russian Defense Ministry reportedly concealed his disappearance for months before formally notifying police in May 2026, launching a search across the Leningrad region.

RAF receives Saab Giraffe 1X radars for drone defence
United Kingdom
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-02
10:13:55 BST
18:13:55 KST

Saab UK has delivered Giraffe 1X radar systems to the Royal Air Force for use in counter-drone operations, with the equipment intended to support the detection and tracking of uncrewed aerial systems on deployed operations.
The delivery follows what Saab described as an urgent operational requirement from the RAF and builds on previous work between the company and the service on counter-UAS capability. Saab said the radars have now become part of the RAF’s wider counter-drone architecture, supporting the detection, tracking and engagement of airborne threats alongside other systems used to protect personnel and facilities.
A Royal Air Force spokesperson said: “As the customer, we have been impressed with how Saab were able to mobilise their global production capacity to rapidly satisfy our Giraffe 1X requirement in support of Counter Drone operations on deployed operations. This equipment is critical in mitigating the risk to life posed by the drone threat. Saab gave delivery quickly and innovatively, working with the MOD team to satisfy this contract.”
Saab said the procurement was driven by an operational requirement and involved cooperation between its UK operations and the company’s wider production network. The company did not give the number of Giraffe 1X systems delivered, the value of the procurement or the precise locations at which the radars will be operated.
The Giraffe 1X is a compact three-dimensional radar designed for short-range surveillance and the detection of small airborne targets. Saab markets the system for roles including counter-UAS, ground-based air defence and battlefield surveillance, with the radar designed to be deployed from fixed positions or integrated onto vehicles and other mobile platforms.
Andy Fraser, Group Managing Director at Saab UK, said: “This delivery showcases the dedication and expertise of teams across Saab, from our UK manufacturing operations through to colleagues across the wider business, who worked together to support delivery of this capability. It demonstrates the strength of Saab’s industrial footprint in the UK and our ability to bring together the right resources to support our customers’ requirements. We are proud to provide British and coalition forces with the capabilities they need to carry out their mission and to keep people and society safe.”
Giraffe 1X is the smallest member of Saab’s Giraffe radar family. According to Saab, the system is designed to detect small, low and slow-moving targets while remaining sufficiently compact for rapid deployment. The radar can also contribute tracking data to wider command-and-control and air defence systems rather than operating as a standalone counter-drone weapon.

18:13:48 KST

Arnaldo Pomodoro’s “Sfera Grande” has returned to public view in Tehran after undergoing conservation and restoration work that lasted over a year.
                                    
                                       
				The event, attended on behalf of the embassy by First Secretary Emanuele Marchi, who is responsible for cultural affairs, helped commemorate the centennial of the birth of the renowned Italian artist, who last visited Tehran over 20 years ago. The anniversary, which falls this year, was also commemorated with a limited-edition postage stamp featuring an image of the restored sculpture.
                                    
                                       
				The bronze sculpture, weighing 3,000 kilograms and measuring approximately 3 meters in diameter—part of a limited series of similar works, including its exact twin located in front of the Palazzo della Farnesina—was created by the Italian artist in 1974 on commission from the Shah’s wife, Farah Diba, and transported to Iran in 1978. The restoration of the work was spearheaded by the Dafineh Museums Group, a leading public institution that manages—in addition to the Museum of Time—the Iran Art Museum, the Iran Historic Automobile Museum, the Yazd Museum of Light and Illumination, the National Museum of Arts in Isfahan, and the Ramsar Complex.

World Food Programme halves food assistance to West Bank due to funding shortages
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-02
09:12:51 UTC
18:12:51 KST

The World Food Programme (WFP) is cutting in half the number of Palestinians it can support with food assistance in the West Bank due to funding shortfalls, the UN program announced Tuesday.
Despite now reducing the service, the WFP shared that food needs have doubled since 2023 and an estimated 900,000 people are experiencing food insecurity in the Palestinian territory, and up until now the program has only been able to support 400,000 of those in need.
While not mentioned by the WFP, after Hamas’s October 7 attacks on southern Israel, the Israeli work permits of 140,000 Palestinian was revoked.
WFP’s latest quarterly food security analysis found that 76% of households in the West Bank have experienced a significant decline in income, and the food and fuel prices remain among the highest in the Middle East. These prices, the WFP claimed, have forced many families to sell assets and reduce the number and quality of their meals to survive.
Notably, according to the Palestinian Central Bureau of Statistics, the unemployment rate among those aged 15 and above stood at 27.9%, and the average daily wage stands at only NIS 134.3, just over half of Israel’s minimum daily wage of NIS 257.75.
One-third of West Bank Palestinian families cannot afford nutritious diet
The WFP’s analysis also noted that around 12% of Palestinians in the West Bank have poor food consumption and around a third of families cannot afford a nutritious diet, especially those living in rural areas and in the southern West Bank.
“Families who were once thriving and earning a living from their land are now unable to afford enough food,” said Shaun Hughes, WFP Country Director for the Palestinian territories. “At a time when WFP should be scaling up assistance to reach more people, we are being forced to make difficult decisions, prioritizing the most vulnerable while cutting assistance to others despite widespread needs. We urge the international community to act immediately and step up support for Palestinians.”
Operations in Gaza are also being affected by the funding shortfall. In July, the WFP reduced by 40% the cash value of its assistance for 375,000 people.

FACTBOX - What SCO leaders signed at Bishkek summit
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-02
09:12:11 UTC
18:12:11 KST

- Leaders adopt post-summit declaration, reaffirming their commitment to SCO Charter, as well as to further strengthen good-neighborliness, friendship, multidisciplinary cooperation
- Beyond declaration, leaders also sign more than 20 other documents covering security, drug trafficking, technology, transport, energy, environmental cooperation
Kyrgyzstan hosted the latest summit of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) in its capital, Bishkek, marking the Eurasian bloc's 25th anniversary.
Following a meeting of the Council of Heads of State, the organization's 10 member states adopted key documents covering security, drug trafficking, technology, transport, energy and environmental cooperation.
A key post-summit declaration was also adopted, reaffirming the member states' commitment to the organization’s charter, as well as their commitment to further strengthening good-neighborliness, friendship and multidisciplinary cooperation.
Here are some important details about the documents adopted:
According to the Bishkek Declaration, the text of which has been published by the Kremlin, the member states voiced appreciation for the organization's achievements in ensuring regional security and stability.
It highlighted member states’ position that the SCO is not a military-political bloc and is not directed against other states or international organizations.
“The SCO operates on the basis of openness, non-interference, equality and mutual respect,” it said.
The document further said that the organization welcomed cooperation with “interested states, international organizations and multilateral associations whose activities are not directed against the interests of the SCO and its member states.”
In this context, the document underlined cooperation in the SCO Plus format, which includes non-members such as Türkiye, Azerbaijan and Egypt, as facilitating the formation of a “broad, inclusive global partnership.”
It also stressed the importance of further strengthening the SCO's dialogue with the UN.
The document also reaffirmed the need to conclude an “international legally binding instrument” to ensure transparency and provide reliable guarantees against an arms race in outer space.
“Member states reiterate that the unilateral and unlimited buildup of global missile defense systems by individual countries or groups of states has a negative impact on international security and stability,” the document said, defining attempts by states to ensure their own security at the expense of the security of others as “unacceptable.”
They also advocated strict adherence to the Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons and called for full compliance with the Chemical Weapons Convention.
They expressed “deep concern” over developments in the Middle East and around Iran, advocating a resolution to the conflict solely through political and diplomatic means.
“Member states note that the only possible way to ensure peace and stability in the Middle East is a comprehensive and just settlement of the Palestinian question,” it said, adding that they also reaffirm their commitment to combating terrorism, separatism and extremism.
The bloc's chairmanship will pass to Pakistan.
Aside from the post-summit declaration, the SCO also adopted 27 other documents covering security, drug trafficking, technology, transport, energy and environmental cooperation between member states.
A statement by the Kyrgyz presidency on the outcomes of the summit said that the documents adopted included a protocol on amendments and additions to the SCO Charter, which was adopted in the Russian city of St. Petersburg in June 2002.
The statement said that documents were adopted on regulations concerning the Universal Center for Countering Challenges and Threats to the Security of SCO Member States and the Executive Committee of the SCO Anti-Drug Center.
Another key document mentioned was an action plan for the development of ports and logistics centers of the member states for 2026-2030.
Notably, documents were also signed on declaring Pakistan's city of Lahore as the tourist and cultural capital of the SCO in 2026-2027, as well as on the development of cooperation in the field of energy conservation, efficiency and systems, and on providing assistance to states affected by emergency situations.
A memorandum of understanding was also signed between the SCO Secretariat and the African Union Commission.
It also noted that memorandums were adopted between the governments of SCO member states on cooperation in the information sphere, as well as in combating climate change and in the field of artificial intelligence.
It added that a protocol on amendments and supplements to a 2010 agreement on cooperation between the governments of SCO member states in combating crime was also signed.

Swiss-based ADAPT latest hedge fund to open Abu Dhabi office

Swiss-based ADAPT latest hedge fund to open Abu Dhabi office
Swiss hedge fund ADAPT Investment Managers has become the latest among a slew of peers opening an office in Abu Dhabi as the emirate continues to attract financial firms despite the ongoing conflict in the Middle East.
The $2 billion relative-value hedge fund has started operations in the Gulf city, according to a statement from the firm on Wednesday. The new base, which will be led by Daniel Mullarkey who recently joined as a senior research analyst, is the money manager’s fourth office, after Geneva and Zug in Switzerland, and New York.
ADAPT has separately bolstered its ranks with a clutch of hires from a few of the industry’s largest multi-strategy hedge fund firms. Those coming on board as portfolio managers include Nicolas Dumoulin and Olivier Chazalon, formerly with Millennium Management and Verition Fund Management, respectively. Fabien Gerbron, who previously worked for Citadel, joined recently.
Abu Dhabi, along with neighboring Dubai, has drawn significant interest from global investment firms for its deep sovereign wealth reserves and attractive tax regime. But the outbreak of conflict in the region this year has raised questions about their appeal as financial hubs.
But there are signs of continued interest even after the outbreak of hostilities. Chris Rokos’ hedge fund firm reaffirmed its commitment to Abu Dhabi earlier this year, securing a full regulatory license to operate in the city. Hudson Bay Capital Management, along with Marshall Wace and Brevan Howard Asset Management, are among other industry heavyweights already operating there.
The ADAPT fund launched in March 2020 and managed $2.11 billion at the start of August this year, according to an investor letter seen by Bloomberg News. The fund made 1.77% in July, erasing year-to-date losses to gain 0.23% over the first seven months of the year, it showed.

The Democratic Republic of the Congo’s Ebola outbreak has killed more than 3,000 people out of more than 6,100 confirmed cases, according to the latest government data released on Wednesday, as the disease continues to spread rapidly.
Data from the DRC’s Ministry of Health showed that 6,186 confirmed cases and 3,007 deaths had been recorded since the outbreak was declared on May 15.
The outbreak, caused by the Bundibugyo variant of Ebola, is the fastest-growing outbreak of the disease on record, according to the government data.
There are currently no approved vaccines or treatments for the Bundibugyo strain.
The outbreak has intensified since it was first declared, while weak health infrastructure, community resistance, instability and protests by response workers have hampered efforts to identify and contain cases.

Cargo ship with 10 crew members sinks off Istanbul after collision with vessel
- A Turkish cargo ship, Tugberk Imamoglu, sank quickly after colliding with the empty oil tanker ALSU near Istanbul's Marmara Sea.
- Ten crew members are missing; search and rescue efforts involve 14 vessels and a helicopter but no survivors have been found so far.
- The cargo ship carried 4,200 tons of rolled steel, and the incident happened just days after another deadly ferry accident in the region.
AI generated
ISTANBUL – A Turkish cargo ship sank in the Marmara Sea near Istanbul after colliding with a second vessel, with rescuers searching for its 10 crew members, Turkish officials said on Sept 2.
The incident occurred before dawn when the Alsu, an empty oil tanker, collided with the Tugberk Imamoglu, a cargo ship carrying rolled steel, which sank shortly after, the transport ministry’s maritime directorate said on X.
“Due to the Tugberk Imamoglu not responding to any calls and the crew not answering their mobile phones... it is believed the dry cargo ship has sunk,” it said.
The collision occurred 18 nautical miles off Silivri district on the western edge of Istanbul province, with Transport Minister Abdulkadir Uraloglu telling journalists the damaged vessel had sunk “very quickly”.
“We received the emergency call at 0326. If we accept the captain’s reported time of 0315, we can say the sinking occurred very rapidly, within just 11 minutes.
“We spotted life buoys and a lifeboat but it was empty. Unfortunately, no survivors have been found so far. Search and rescue operations are continuing by sea and air,” he said.
He said there were 10 people on board: the captain and nine crew members, all of them Turkish nationals.
The cargo ship went down in waters that were approximately 900m deep, with 14 vessels and a helicopter involved in search and rescue efforts, the maritime directorate said.
“Life-saving equipment, including a lifeboat belonging to the Tugberk Imamoglu which had 10 crew members on board, has been found at sea. Unfortunately, the crew members were not inside,” it said.
The Alsu, which was damaged in the collision, was also participating in search and rescue efforts, it said.
According to the VesselFinder tracking website, the Tugberk Imamoglu is a Turkish-flagged cargo ship built in 1990 which is 90m long.
At the time of the collision, it was carrying 4,200 tons of rolled sheet metal and rebar, the authorities said.
The maritime directorate initially said the Alsu was carrying 3,000 tonnes of motor oil, but later said the tanker was empty in a detail confirmed by the governorate.
The incident took place three days after a deadly ferry accident off Northern Cyprus in which eight Turkish nationals died, with rescuers still hunting for another 20 people listed as missing. AFP

====================================================================================================

From Sushant Singh Rajput 'link' to CBI probe: The Disha Salian case so far
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-02
09:10:45 UTC
18:10:45 KST

The Bombay High Court on Wednesday ordered a CBI investigation into Disha Salian’s death, citing concerns over the prolonged police probe and failure to register an FIR
NEW DELHI: The Bombay High Court on Wednesday ordered the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) to register an FIR and take over the investigation into the death of Disha Salian, former manager of actor Sushant Singh Rajput, who died in June 2020.A bench of Justices Sarang Kotwal and Ranjitsinha Raja Bhonsale directed Mumbai Police to hand over all case records to the CBI and ordered that the probe be conducted by a suitably experienced and senior officer.The court also pulled up Mumbai Police over the manner and duration of its investigation, saying it had continued for about six years without an FIR being registered. The bench observed that the police investigation “raises more questions than it answers” and said a CBI probe was necessary.The 44-page judgment said there were “glaring discrepancies” in the police investigation and called for a “proper and substantive” probe.“In this case, we are of the opinion that the police had sufficient opportunity to investigate the offence, but they have not registered the FIR and have not carried out the investigation of a cognisable offence,” the court said.Reacting to the order, Salian’s father Satish Salian, who has pursued the case for six years and alleged that his daughter was murdered, said he felt “relieved” but had no reason to celebrate after losing his daughter.
“I have been waiting for this for 6 years. There is no reason to be happy. I have lost my daughter. I feel relieved today. That's all,” he told reporters, adding that he had folded his hands and thanked the judge.
What is the case?
Disha Salian was found dead on June 8, 2020, after falling from the 14th floor of a residential building in Mumbai’s Malad area. Mumbai Police registered an Accidental Death Report (ADR) and, after an inquiry, maintained that she had died by suicide.Salian’s father challenged the police’s handling of the case and approached the Bombay High Court, alleging that his daughter had been gang-raped and murdered.He also alleged a politically orchestrated cover-up to protect influential people and sought registration of an FIR and a CBI investigation, including into allegations against Shiv Sena (UBT) MLA Aaditya Thackeray.The high court, however, made it clear that it was not expressing any opinion on the allegations against any individual. It said the CBI would have to determine whether the evidence gathered during its investigation warranted treating anyone as an accused.The court pointed to several aspects of the investigation that it said required closer examination. One issue was the spot panchnama, or the record of the scene where Salian’s body was found, which the court noted had been conducted belatedly.The bench also questioned the absence of blood at the spot. It raised doubts about whether the injuries recorded in the case were consistent with a fall from such a height.“If the deceased had fallen on her face from the 12th floor, then it is difficult to accept that there was only one injury on the chin of the body. Not a single facial bone was fractured. We find this difficult to accept,” the court said, as quoted by PTI.During an earlier hearing, the court had also questioned how a fall from such height could result in such limited injuries. The prosecution had argued that Salian suffered severe facial, skull and rib fractures and that rain could have washed away blood from the spot. The court noted that the rain cited by the prosecution had occurred several hours after the incident.The bench also noted an apparent discrepancy concerning Salian’s clothing. It observed that while the panchnama and post-mortem report stated that her body had no clothes, photographs from the hospital and morgue appeared to show her wearing clothes.“There is room for reasonable doubt in all these aspects. However, we are not drawing any conclusion at this stage,” the court said.The court had also earlier questioned why Mumbai Police had registered only an ADR despite the allegations raised by Salian’s family. It noted that copies of the post-mortem report and ADR had not been provided to the family even years after her death.Salian’s lawyer Nilesh Ojha had alleged discrepancies in the post-mortem report and argued that an FIR should have been registered on the basis of the allegations and material placed before the authorities.
What has the HC ordered?
The High Court directed the CBI to record Satish Salian’s statement and register an FIR. Mumbai Police was ordered to hand over all papers and records relating to the case to the central agency “forthwith”.The CBI has been asked to appoint a suitably experienced and senior officer to investigate the case.The court also imposed an important safeguard: no individual can be treated as an accused merely on the basis of the allegations made before the court.“Nobody shall be treated as an accused unless in the opinion of the investigating officer there are sufficient grounds to raise reasonable suspicion against him depending on the material collected during the investigation,” the court said.The bench also said that if the investigation finds that no criminal case is made out, the CBI must file an appropriate summary report before the competent court.“In case the investigation reveals that no case is made out, then the CBI shall file the appropriate summary report before the court concerned,” it said.Satish Salian will be free to challenge such a report and file objections before the court.The high court described Salian as an “unfortunate” father who had lost his young daughter in “tragic circumstances” and said the matter required a substantive investigation. At the same time, it refrained from commenting on the allegations made against specific individuals.Satish Salian’s petition sought an FIR and investigation into allegations against Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Aaditya Thackeray, son of former Maharashtra chief minister Uddhav Thackeray.The court however did not make any adverse finding against Thackeray and said it was for the investigating agency to examine the evidence.Thackeray had separately approached the high court seeking to intervene in the proceedings. In his application, he described Satish Salian’s petition as “false, frivolous and motivated” and sought an opportunity to be heard before any order was passed.
The case has also drawn attention because Salian had briefly worked as a manager for actor Sushant Singh Rajput.Rajput was found dead at his Bandra residence on June 14, 2020, six days after Salian’s death. The proximity of the two deaths led to widespread speculation, although the cases were investigated separately.A CBI probe was also ordered into Rajput’s death. The agency subsequently filed a closure report stating that he died by suicide; the concerned court is yet to decide on the report.The latest order does not establish that Salian was murdered or that the allegations made by her family are true. It instead directs a fresh investigation by the CBI after finding that the police probe contained issues that, in the court’s view, warranted further examination.

Russian senior diplomat discusses Arctic, NATO’s preps for military conflict with Moscow
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-02
09:10:33 UTC
18:10:33 KST

VLADIVOSTOK, September 2. /TASS/. NATO countries are gearing up for a military conflict with Moscow, Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Alexander Grushko said at the Eastern Economic Forum (EEF).
He also pointed out that the West had declared the Arctic a zone of geopolitical competition and is determined to secure military superiority there.
TASS has compiled the key statements made by the senior Russian diplomat.
Black Sea proposals
The Kiev regime seeks a stop-gap solution on a Black Sea ceasefire to gain a respite, but this will not work: "Stop-gap solutions are not going to work as the [Kiev] regime will only take advantage of them to have a respite and regroup its forces."
NATO’s preparations for conflict with Russia
The North Atlantic Alliance’s countries are making preparations for a military conflict with Russia: "They are really moving toward military confrontation with Russia. It’s not so much about rhetoric but, if we use professional terms and look at everything they say and do, it’s about preparations for war with Russia."
Under any scenario involving NATO countries, Russia will reliably ensure the security of its borders: "We have all the necessary means to reliably protect our interests and ensure our combat capacity and border security under any scenario."
Possible resumption of grain deal
The terms of the grain deal concerning access for Russian products to international markets were never fulfilled: "An essential part of it [the deal] was not implemented. Nothing was done to ensure market access for Russian grain and Russian fertilizers or to make payments possible. Everything was swept under the rug, so the deal was officially dead."
However, the West still has not changed its stance on sanctions: "Have you seen any changes in the West’s position on sanctions? I personally haven’t."
Arctic situation
The West has unleashed a hybrid war against Russia in the North but will never be able to achieve military superiority: "I would certainly like to point out that as for objective and very constructive cooperation, the West will seek to create barriers. A hybrid war has been unleashed against our country and as far as the North goes, it’s not only about military confrontation but also the desire to ensure and achieve military superiority, which they will never be able to do for numerous reasons, as well as to use various other means."
The West has declared the Arctic a zone of geopolitical competition and is seeking to gain military superiority there: "Today we can see clearly that Western countries have declared the Arctic region a zone of geopolitical competition. Until recently, for some reason, they did not make any announcements about this, but now they have suddenly decided that it’s a zone of geopolitical competition and that in order to be competitive in the higher latitudes, the West needs to achieve military superiority."
Baltic Sea situation
NATO’s activities in recent years have turned the Baltic Sea, once a calm region, into an area of military confrontation: "The situation in the Baltic region and the Baltic Sea is telling, as activities by the West, NATO, the European Union and the United States have in a few years turned this calm region, where there was no military agenda at all, into an actual zone of not just military competition but also military confrontation, where the risk of unexpected military incidents is extremely high, and tensions have a tendency to escalate, particularly spiraling out of control."
Germany’s policies
Moscow will respond to Germany’s move to shut down the Russian consulate in Bonn: "We will respond in a way we see fit and when we are ready. I think it won’t take long but will happen very soon."
Germany has opted "for a path of escalation that excludes nothing on the diplomatic track."
Northern Sea Route
The scale of container traffic along the Northern Sea Route is set to grow in geometric, rather than arithmetic, progression: "This year marks an important milestone as major container traffic was launched between Asia and Europe. It’s perfectly clear that the scale of traffic will grow not in arithmetic but in geometric progression."

Range Rover launches its first electric vehicle, with starting price of £154,070
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-02
09:08:23 UTC
18:08:23 KST

Range Rover has launched its first electric vehicle – a year later than planned – offering a greener option for fans of gargantuan British-made SUVs who are also conscious about the climate crisis.
Due to be built in Solihull, the home of the marque since 1970, the vehicle comes with an eye-watering price tag, starting at £154,070.
However, the delayed launch marks a milestone departure from cars powered by fossil fuels for Jaguar Land Rover (JLR), which is owned by India’s Tata Motors but headquartered in Coventry in the UK.
It also provides a much-needed moment of positivity for JLR, which reported falling profits earlier this year as it counted the cost of Donald Trump’s tariff wars and supply chain disruption after a crippling cyber-attack last year.
JLR said it had given extra training to 10,500 staff working on the project and that the car had undergone testing equivalent to 38 trips around the world, more than any other Range Rover.
The company said the luxury vehicle, which can reach 60mph in 4.3 seconds, heralded “a new era of enhanced refinement and capability”.
While the model’s electric powertrain will limit its impact on the environment compared with JLR’s petrol and diesel models, SUVs of its size are consistently linked to higher numbers of road deaths in accidents involving pedestrians.
However, Ranger Rover’s bespoke commissioning service does mean that buyers have an “extended choice of near limitless paint colours and finishes, elevated materials, tailored colour combinations and personalisation details including unique embroidery”.
Martin Limpert, the managing director of Range Rover, said the vehicle was the end product of a “decade of considered engineering and technological development”.
Production at Solihull will be supported by the automaker’s propulsion manufacturing centre, in Wolverhampton, which makes battery packs and electric drive units, as well as traditional internal combustion engines.

Ryanair cuts passenger target as high fuel costs prompt smaller winter schedule
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-02
09:07:19 UTC
18:07:19 KST

Mucahithan Avcioglu
02 September 2026•Update: 02 September 2026
- Sustained fuel costs could materially raise European short-haul fares and threaten less-hedged rivals, company warns
Ryanair lowered its passenger target for the current financial year as soaring jet fuel prices prompted the Irish budget airline to reduce its winter schedule.
The carrier said Wednesday that it now expects to carry 214 million passengers in fiscal 2027, down from its previous forecast of 216 million.
The reduction is intended to limit Ryanair’s exposure to unhedged fuel purchases during its typically loss-making winter schedule from November to March.
Passenger traffic during that period is now expected to remain broadly unchanged from a year earlier.
Ryanair said the one-off schedule reduction could cut its winter losses by between €70 million ($81 million) and €100 million, depending on pricing and passenger demand.
Jet fuel was trading at approximately $140 per barrel, according to the company, as the conflict in the Middle East continued to drive energy prices higher.
Ryanair has hedged 80% of its fuel requirements for fiscal 2027 at around $67 per barrel, providing it with greater protection against elevated spot prices than many competitors.
The airline said it remains well positioned to record another profitable year, although profit after tax is expected to fall below the record level achieved in fiscal 2026. 
It added that it was still too early to provide detailed profit guidance.
Ryanair also warned that European short-haul airfares could rise materially if high oil prices persist into the summer 2027 season, as airlines pass increased fuel costs on to passengers.
Some less-hedged competitors could struggle to maintain capacity or even survive the coming winter, it added.
Despite the revised full-year target, Ryanair remains on course to increase its summer traffic by more than 5% to 145 million passengers from 138 million a year earlier.
The airline carried 22.2 million passengers in August, up 6% from 21 million in the same month last year, while its load factor remained unchanged at 96%.
Rolling 12-month traffic increased 5% to 214.4 million passengers, with the load factor steady at 94%.

Chinese researchers crack tough challenge of low-grade iron ore utilization
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-02
17:06:02 CST
18:06:02 KST

BEIJING, Sept. 2 (Xinhua) -- For decades, billions of tonnes of iron-bearing mine tailings in China lay largely unused. Zhu Qingshan, a researcher at the Institute of Process Engineering (IPE) under the Chinese Academy of Sciences, once said: "Turning this 'sleeping wealth' into usable high-grade resources is key to solving the country's iron ore supply problem."
That vision has now become reality. On Tuesday, the world's largest iron ore magnetization roasting project, with an annual capacity of 5.56 million tonnes, passed official acceptance tests in Anshan, northeast China's Liaoning Province. It has been operating stably at full capacity, with key performance indicators exceeding design targets. The project marks a major breakthrough in the industrial use of low-grade iron ore.
According to the IPE, the technology is the world's first solution for large-scale industrial processing of ultra-low-grade iron tailings. It can turn tailings with an iron content of just 11 percent into concentrate with a grade of 65 percent.
This breakthrough is expected to enable efficient and green development and utilization of nearly 30 billion tonnes of refractory iron ore and almost 10 billion tonnes of iron-bearing tailings in China, the IPE said.
HALF-CENTURY QUEST
China consumes more than half of the world's iron ore. Although domestic reserves are abundant, most of the country's deposits are low-grade and hard to process with conventional methods. Over the past decade, China has imported 11.3 billion tonnes of iron ore. Tapping underused domestic resources has driven generations of researchers to tackle this long-standing technical challenge.
In the 1950s, the Institute of Chemical Metallurgy, the IPE's predecessor, began exploring ways to make efficient use of low-grade iron ore. Chemical engineer Mooson Kwauk pioneered fluidized-bed magnetizing roasting techniques to convert poor-quality iron minerals into recoverable magnetite.
Although the technology showed promise, its industrialization was interrupted due to the country's weak industrial base and the historical conditions at the time. Researcher Zhu Qingshan later took up the unfinished mission.
In 2004, Zhu began devoting himself to research on refractory iron ore. At that time, the technology still faced major hurdles to industrialization: conventional magnetizing roasting suffered from low reaction efficiency, high energy consumption and costs, and poor operational stability. Zhu's team introduced innovative technical approaches to address these issues and lay the groundwork for practical application.
FROM LAB TO INDUSTRIAL SCALE
For Zhu, successful basic research was not the end, but the starting point for industrial application. To turn research into usable technology, Zhu and his team developed a complete system for fluidized-bed magnetizing roasting, including key equipment and supporting technologies.
The team secured a partner in southwest China's Yunnan Province for a project with an annual capacity of 100,000 tonnes. However, the project stalled in 2008 amid the global financial crisis due to funding shortages. With support from various levels of government, the researchers spent more than a year troubleshooting on site, and the plant achieved continuous stable operation in December 2012.
This experience also exposed new limitations in the technology, prompting the team to further improve the roasting process and energy efficiency. They developed a second-generation magnetizing roasting process with more precise control of particle residence time, which was later introduced to Ansteel Group, one of China's major steelmakers.
At Ansteel, the technology has achieved a 98-percent conversion rate for iron minerals, delivering significant economic benefits. Eleven licensing agreements now cover a combined annual processing capacity of more than 15 million tonnes. The team is also advancing overseas projects, including a limonite upgrading initiative in Laos. Looking ahead, researchers plan to extend the technology to other mineral processing and solid-waste recycling applications. ■
